back_translation: On my bed in the night I sought the one my heart loves; I sought him, but did not find him.
I will arise right now and go around the city, through the streets and the city squares; I will seek the one my heart loves. I sought him, but did not find him.
The watchmen making their rounds of the city found me. I asked, “Have you seen the one my heart loves?”
Scarcely had I passed them when I found the one my heart loves. I embraced him and would not let go until I had brought him into my mother's house, into the chamber of her who gave me birth.
O daughters of Jerusalem, I make you swear by the gazelles and the does of the field: do not stir up or awaken love until love itself pleases.
Who is that coming up from the wilderness like a column of smoke, fragrant with myrrh and frankincense, from all the spices of the merchant?
Behold, it is Solomon's royal litter, surrounded by sixty mighty men from the mighty men of Israel.
All of them skilled with the sword, experienced in war, each with his sword at his thigh, ready against the terror of the night.
King Solomon made the royal carriage for himself from the wood of Lebanon.
Its posts he made of silver, its base of gold, its seat upholstered in purple cloth, its interior adorned with love by the daughters of Jerusalem.
Come out, O daughters of Zion, and look upon King Solomon wearing the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his royal wedding, the day of the gladness of his heart.
